'''Hinohonome Shrine''' is a shrine in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Bungo Province]].

Ōita|war|Beppu, Ōita|zh|別府市|zh_classical|別府市|zh_min_nan|Beppu-chhī|zh_yue|別府|qid=Q273880|lt=Beppu City}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}, and its former shrine Rank was that of a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社}}, as categorized under the modern shrine Ranking system (see {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}{{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Various Shrines}}).

It consists of three shrines:
- Upper Shrine (Oku-no-miya) located at the summit of {{ill|Mount Tsurumi|arz|جبل مونت تسورومى|ceb|Tsurumi Dake|fr|Mont Tsurumi|ja|鶴見岳|qid=Q6924219|lt=Tsurumi-yama}},
- Middle Shrine (Higashiyama) on the mid-slope (also known as '''Mitake Gongen''' <おたけごんげん>),
- Lower Shrine (Sato-no-miya) at the foot (also known as '''Tsurumi Gongen''').

== Worshipped Deities (Saijin) ==
{{see also|{{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saijin}}}}
* Upper Shrine: {{ill|Hinokagutsuchi no Mikoto|ja|火之加具土命}} (ほのかぐつちのみこと), and Hiyaki Hayame no Mikoto (ひやきはやめのみこと)
* Middle Shrine: Hinokagutsuchi no Mikoto, and Hiyaki Hayame no Mikoto
* Lower Shrine: {{ill|Izanagi|en|Izanagi|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagi}}, {{ill|Izanami|en|Izanami|qid=Q682306|lt=Izanami}}, Hinokagutsuchi no Kami (火之加具土神), and {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|en|Ōyamatsumi|qid=Q386563|qid=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi}}

== History ==
=== Founding ===
According to shrine tradition, the enshrinement was established in {{ill|771|ja|771}} (Hōki 2, {{ill|Hōki|de|Hōki (Ära)|es|Hōki (nengō)|fa|هوکی (دوره)|fr|Ère Hōki|ia|Hoki (era)|id|Hōki|ja|宝亀|ko|호키 (연호)|pt|Hōki (era)|ru|Хоки (нэнго)|simple|Hōki|sr|Хоки|tr|Hōki|uk|Хокі|zh|寶龜|zh_yue|寶龜|qid=Q18520676|lt=宝亀}} 2).

The deities that give the shrine its name, {{ill|Hinokagutsuchi no Mikoto|ja|火之加具土命}} and Hiyaki Hayame no Mikoto (火焼速女命), are thought to be the deification of the two peaks of {{ill|Sacred mountains|en|Sacred mountains|qid=Q1595289|lt=Sacred Mountain}} ({{ill|Mount Tsurumi|arz|جبل مونت تسورومى|ceb|Tsurumi Dake|fr|Mont Tsurumi|ja|鶴見岳|qid=Q6924219|lt=Tsurumi-yama}}) into male and female deities. It was widely known from ancient times that there were {{ill|Onsen|en|Onsen|qid=Q655311|lt=Onsen}} at the foot of {{ill|Mount Tsurumi|arz|جبل مونت تسورومى|ceb|Tsurumi Dake|fr|Mont Tsurumi|ja|鶴見岳|qid=Q6924219|lt=Tsurumi-yama}} in {{ill|Bungo Province|en|Bungo Province|qid=Q864148|lt=Bungo Province}}'s {{ill|Hayami District, Ōita|ceb|Hayami-gun|de|Hayami-gun|fa|منطقه هایامی، اوئیتا|fr|District de Hayami|id|Distrik Hayami, Ōita|it|Distretto di Hayami|ja|速見郡|ko|하야미군|pl|Powiat Hayami|zh|速見郡|qid=Q1043858|lt=Hayami District}}, but due to the active eruptions of Tsurumi-yama, the area had become barren land and marshes, and was left undeveloped. Both the {{ill|Bungo Fudoki|ja|豊後国風土記}} and the {{ill|Man'yōshū|en|Man'yōshū|qid=Q834321|lt=Man'yōshū}} mention features such as the "Akayu Spring" (赤湯の泉) corresponding to what is now the {{ill|Blood Pond Hell|ja|血の池地獄}} at {{ill|Shibaishi Onsen|ja|柴石温泉}}, and the "Kuberi-yu no I" (玖倍理湯の井) corresponding to the hellish area of {{ill|Tetsunawa Onsen|ja|鉄輪温泉}}. Furthermore, an excerpt from the {{ill|Iyo Fudoki|ja|伊予国風土記}} recounts a {{ill|Myth|en|Myth|qid=Q12827256|lt=myth}} in which {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主命}} directed a conduit from the "Hayami no Yu" ({{ill|Hayami no Yu|ja|速見の湯}}) spring, which emerges at the foot of Tsurumi-yama—the shrine's shintai—to {{ill|Dōgo Onsen|en|Dōgo Onsen|qid=Q1037748|lt=Dōgo Onsen}}, thereby healing the illness of {{ill|Sukunahikona no Mikoto|ja|少彦名命}}.

== Overview ==
According to the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qid=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}<ref group="原" name="貞観9th year 2月26日"/> <ref group="原" name="貞観9th year 4月3日">According to the Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku, entry of April 3, 867 (Jōgan 9).</ref>, when {{ill|867|ja|867}} (Jōgan 9) on {{ill|January 20|en|January 20|qid=Q2267|lt=January 20}}, an eruption occurred at {{ill|Mount Tsurumi|arz|جبل مونت تسورومى|ceb|Tsurumi Dake|fr|Mont Tsurumi|ja|鶴見岳|qid=Q6924219|lt=Tsurumi-yama}}, and at the command of the Court to the provincial governor of {{ill|Bungo Province|en|Bungo Province|qid=Q864148|lt=Bungo Province}}, the {{ill|Large Prajñāpāramitā Sūtras|en|Large Prajñāpāramitā Sūtras|qid=Q15905785|lt=Great Prajna Sutra}} was recited before the shrine.

In {{ill|927|ja|927}} (Enchō 5) the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Jinmyōchō}} was established, wherein the shrine is recorded as "Hinohonome Shrine Two-seat" in {{ill|Bungo Province|en|Bungo Province|qid=Q864148|lt=Bungo Province}}'s {{ill|Hayami District, Ōita|ceb|Hayami-gun|de|Hayami-gun|fa|منطقه هایامی، اوئیتا|fr|District de Hayami|id|Distrik Hayami, Ōita|it|Distretto di Hayami|ja|速見郡|ko|하야미군|pl|Powiat Hayami|zh|速見郡|qid=Q1043858|lt=Hayami District}}, and it is listed among the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} alongside {{ill|Unagi Hime Shrine|ja|宇奈岐日女神社}} in Hayami District.

In {{ill|1276|ja|1276}} (Kenji 2), the itinerant monk {{ill|Ippen|en|Ippen|qid=Q1056232|lt=Ippen}}, who was traveling across Kyushu, is said to have stopped in Beppu and, guided by Tsurumi Gongen, pacified the "Kuberi-yu no I", thereby opening the stone bath (currently known as {{ill|Tetsunawa Mushiyu|ja|鉄輪むし湯}}) at {{ill|Tetsunawa Onsen|ja|鉄輪温泉}}. Consequently, the shrine has been venerated as the guardian deity of the {{ill|Beppu Hachiyu|ja|別府八湯}}.

During the Tenshō era, the shrine buildings were burned by {{ill|Otomo Sōrin|ja|大友宗麟}}, and many ancient documents were lost, but the Lower Shrine was rebuilt in {{ill|1664|ja|1664}} (Kanbun 4) by Kurushima Dōsei. The area around the Lower Shrine, Tsurumi Village, became an exclave of the Mori Domain, and the {{ill|Myōban Onsen|ja|明礬温泉}} produced {{ill|Myōban|ja|明礬}} (also known as {{ill|Onsen Flakes|ja|湯の花}}), which served as an important source of revenue for the domain.

=== Shrine Ranks ===
* In Kakyō 2 ({{ill|849|ja|849}}) on June 1, the deity Hinokahime was accorded the Junior Fifth Rank, Lower. <ref group="原">From the Zoku Nihon Kōki, Kakyō 2, June 1.</ref>
* In Jōgan 9 ({{ill|867|ja|867}}) on February 26, records indicate that the deities {{ill|Hinokami|ja|火男神}} and Honomai were accorded the Junior Fifth Rank, Upper and Lower respectively. <ref group="原" name="貞観9th year 2月26日">From the Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku, entry of February 26, 867.</ref>
* On August 16, 867 (Jōgan 9), both the deity {{ill|Hinokami|ja|火男神}} and the deity {{ill|Honomai|ja|火咩神}}, both of Junior Fifth Rank, Upper, were jointly conferred the Senior Fifth Rank, Lower. <ref group="原" name="貞観9th year 8月16日">From the Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku, entry of August 16, 867.</ref>

== Cultural Properties ==
=== Oita Prefecture Designated Tangible Cultural Properties ===
* The pagoda of the deity of the Sacred Peak at the Middle Shrine – located at the Middle Shrine. Designated on March 28, Showa 50.<ref name="文化財">[http://www.city.beppu.oita.jp/education/shogaigakusyuuka/bunkazai.htm Beppu City's Designated Cultural Properties] (Beppu City Lifelong Learning Division website).</ref>

=== Oita Prefecture Designated Natural Monuments ===
* The Ichiigashi forest of the Tsurumi Gongen Shrine – located at the Lower Shrine. Designated on March 28, Showa 50.<ref name="文化財"/>
* The natural forest of the deity of the Sacred Peak at the Middle Shrine – located at the Middle Shrine. Designated on March 28, Showa 50.<ref name="文化財"/>

Furthermore, the forest of Hinohonome Shrine (Tsurumi, Beppu City) was designated as a specially protected tree area in {{ill|1974|ja|1974}} (Showa 49) on {{ill|March 15|en|March 15|qid=Q2403|lt=March 15}}.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.pref.oita.jp/uploaded/attachment/100227.pdf|title=Oita Prefecture Environmental White Paper|page=44|publisher=Oita Prefecture|accessdate=2024-09-02}}</ref>
